title: Life belongs to the soul in act, not to the body in potency
pass_a_gloss: From the soul comes what comes to be. If the body also is in potency, how can a body that is in potency have life in itself? In other things it is possible to have something and not use it — for example to have sight and not use it — but concerning the soul this is impossible. For not even the sleeper is without psychic activity: he is nourished and grows and imagines and breathes, which is especially proper to life. From these things it is clear that living in potency cannot belong to anything, but always in actuality. For what form-gives the soul is nothing other than the soul itself. Life is connate to the soul; to the body it comes by participation. The one who says health is analogous to life is speaking of the body's life, not the soul's, and so plays the sophist.
pass_b_english: Whatever comes to be comes from the soul. A body that exists only in potency cannot house life by itself. Elsewhere one may possess a power and leave it idle — sight unused — yet the soul admits no such idle possession. Even in sleep psychic work continues: nourishment, growth, imagination, breath, the marks of life. So life is never a mere potency waiting to be switched on; it is always already in act. The soul's form-giving is the soul itself. Life is native to the soul and reaches the body only by share. To treat bodily health as if it were the soul's life is a sophistic slide from body to soul.
source_ref: Wither 1636 OCR pp.~PDF101 (printed ~97); Liber I against soul-as-entelechy
source_text: ἐξ αὐτοῦ τὶ γώεσϑαι. εἰ δὲ καὶ σῶμα δυνάμει ἐστὶ, πῶς πὸ δυνάμει σῶμα δυνάμει ζωὴν ἔχειν ἐν ἑαυτῷ δύναται ἄλλως τὲ, ἐπὶ μὲν τῶν ἄλλων δυνατὸν, ἔχοντά τι, μὴ χρίσϑαι αὐτῷ" οἷον, ὄψιν ἔχοντα, μὴ Χρῆσϑαι αὐτῇ" ἐπὶ δὲ τῆς ψυχῆς ἀδύνατον. οὐδὲ γὰρ ὁ καθεύδων ἄνευ ψυχικῆς ἐνεργείας ἐστί. καὶ γὰρ τρέφεται καὶ αὔξεται καὶ φαντασιοῦται καὶ ἀναπνεῖ, ὅπερ μάλιστα τῆς ζωῦς ἐστι πεκαύριον. ἐκ τούτων οὖν Φανερὲν, ἕτι δυνάμει τὸ ζῆν οὐ φὲ δύναται προςεῖναί τινι, ἀλλὰ πάντως ἐνεργείᾳ. προηγουμέμένως γὰρ τὸ εἰδεποιεῦν τὴν ψυχὴν οὐδὲν ἄλλο ἐστὶν, αλλ᾽ ἃ ἡ ἐμή. τῇ μὲν γὲρ ψυχῇ σὐμφυτός ἐστῶ ἡ ζωή" τῷ δὲ σώματι κατα μέϑεξω. ὁ λέγων τείνυνι τὴν ὑγείαν ἀνά-.
